relevance_note: The paper describes six individually identified patients with de novo GFAP variants: "De novo GFAP mutations in six patients with Alexander disease."
method_note: Read by hand; a short Python script assembled the JSON from my reading, and every span was checked verbatim against the paper. Labels: the text refers to the patients as 'patient 1'..'patient 6' (Table 1 column 'Patient/gender', e.g. '1/M'; Table 2 column 'Patient'), so rule 1 gives 'patient N'. Table 1 has two columns both headed 'GFAP mutation' (cDNA, then protein). Zygosity, de novo inheritance and parental testing come from the named-group statement 'In all six patients ... heterozygous de novo mutation (i.e., not detected in DNA of the parents)'. Variant type and pathogenicity are not stated per variant. Age at last evaluation is the latest age the paper states for that patient's MR investigation (Table 2 for patients 1, 2, 4; Fig. 1 legend for patient 3); for patient 5 (MRI at 6 years, follow-up 'after 2 years', Table 2 at 7 years 5 months) and patient 6 (MRI at 4 years, then 'After 1 year') the age at the last evaluation is not printed as a number, so 'not reported'. No age at symptom onset is given; MRI ages are recorded only as onset of the MRI finding. Patients 1, 3 and 6 are deceased (age at death not stated); patients 2 and 5 are described as clinically stable, but vital status is not stated, so 'not reported'. Patient 2: the initial MRI at 2 years showed abnormalities 'without swelling and without frontal predominance'; later the frontal abnormalities became more marked. Recorded as excluded at the initial MRI and observed later (a change over time, not a contradiction). Group statements not used for individual rows: 'In the white matter of all Alexander patients, high values of ADC were observed, and both FA and MTR were attenuated' (only some patients had DTI/MTI), and qualitative MRS changes ('marked reduction ... tNAA', 'strong elevation ... Ins', 'Cho ... elevated in most measurements'); Table 2 numeric values were not interpreted per patient. Elevated lactate is recorded for patients 1, 2, 3, 4 and 6 from 'The elevated lactate in the affected white matter, observed in all our patients'; patient 5 has an individual statement (Fig. 2 legend). Checklist 'periventricular rim' is marked observed for patients 4 and 5 from 'a thin periventricular rim of lowered ADC values' (a diffusion finding, not the T1/T2 signal rim described in the Introduction); this is a judgement call. Patient 4's 'secondary dilatation of the lateral ventricles' due to atrophy was not taken as hydrocephalus. Control subjects (25 males, 16 females) are out of scope. No stacked cells and no contradictions found.
